bkr.row_text: deadlock: three or more clients/servers closing a cycle through a relay

axes.trap: hmi has a receive window, but only between its own requests

states.bkrdb: SEND (owner query to hmi, which is REPLY-blocked)

bkr.culprit: dbd.c: on a cache miss (key >= 5) it MsgSends to hmi while serving hmi's own request relayed by gw: hmi -> gw -> dbd -> hmi
bkr.fix: answer the miss without calling back into the requester (reply with 'unknown' / look the owner up elsewhere), or let hmi serve owner queries in a separate thread

c3n.row_text: priority_chain: low thread holds a mutex without priority inheritance while a middle thread runs

axes.trap: middle thread is a spin-wait, not a declared load; stats has no log

c3n.culprit: camsvc.c: frame_mx is PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE; dma (6) wakes stats (12) while holding frame_mx, stats spins on dma_done which only dma can set
c3n.fix: make frame_mx PRIO_INHERIT and replace the busy-wait in stats() with a condvar wait signalled by dma after unlocking

cnu.row_text: deadlock: ring of synchronous sends, every member TICKs before its first send

axes.trap: each stage TICKs 3 warm-up rounds before the first send; comment claims downstream acks immediately

states.cnuacq: SEND (MsgSend to the next stage; that stage is itself SEND-blocked and never receives)
states.cnuscl: SEND (MsgSend to the next stage; that stage is itself SEND-blocked and never receives)
states.cnuenc: SEND (MsgSend to the next stage; that stage is itself SEND-blocked and never receives)

cnu.culprit: stage.c main loop: every stage calls qd_send(down) before qd_receive(chid); 3-stage ring acq->scl->enc->acq
cnu.fix: break the ring: receive in a separate thread (or let one stage receive first), or forward with a pulse / MsgDeliverEvent instead of a blocking MsgSend

cv4.row_text: deadlock: server pool exhaustion (every pool thread in a synchronous send back to a client waiting for the pool)

axes.trap: works for 8 rounds; both requests refresh together after a barrier

states.cv4wa: SEND (visibility query to the ui channel; the ui's only receiver is itself sending)
states.cv4r1: REPLY (REFRESH held by a pool thread)
states.cv4ev: SEND (HEADER request to catalogd; no pool thread is receiving)

cv4.culprit: catalogd.c worker(): on REFRESH each pool thread sends synchronously back to the ui, whose only receiving thread (ui.c events()) sends HEADER to the same exhausted pool
cv4.fix: do not call back into the client from a pool thread (reply first and notify with MsgDeliverEvent/pulse), or have events() never block on catalogd (async header fetch), or size the pool above the number of concurrent refreshes plus one

e8s.row_text: unknown: single process ticks a few times, then spins on the CPU

axes.trap: no blocking state at all

states.e8sprs: READY (spins in the TLV loop; preempted only by the observer's pidin on the one core)

e8s.culprit: parser.c main loop: a zero-length field hits 'continue' without advancing off (frame 6)
e8s.fix: advance off by 2 on an empty field before continuing

epe.row_text: deadlock: three or more clients/servers closing a cycle through a relay

axes.trap: broker comment calls single-threading deliberate

states.epekeys: SEND (route registration to the broker, which is REPLY-blocked)

epe.culprit: keys.c: after the 6th signature it MsgSends a route registration to the single-threaded broker while the broker waits on auth -> keys
epe.fix: register routes asynchronously (pulse) or after replying, or give the broker a separate thread for registrations

euf.row_text: healthy: client/server exchange next to a non-messaging CPU load (one above, one below the server)

axes.trap: load priority above the server's base priority

states.eufgps: NANOSLEEP (150 ms per request, running at nav's inherited priority 25)
states.eufmap: READY (CPU load at 15; preempted only by the observer)

euf.culprit: none (gpsd base priority 8 < mapgen 15, but it receives at nav's priority 25 through priority inheritance)

exw.row_text: healthy: looks stuck in one snapshot but keeps ticking

axes.trap: receiver never replies itself; reply comes from the flush thread

states.exwfl: CONDVAR (250 ms timed wait, then replies to the batch)

exw.culprit: none (timer-driven batch replies from another thread)

f82.row_text: priority_chain: high client waits on a qd_fixed_chan server kept off the CPU by a middle load

axes.trap: relay in the middle runs fine (prio 14 > load)

f82.culprit: eeprom.c: qd_fixed_chan server at 4 behind the relay bus is starved by scrub at 12
f82.fix: use an inheriting channel for eeprom (the relay's inherited 35 would then carry through), or raise eeprom above scrub

g2h.row_text: unknown, info_insufficient: loop stops for a cause not in the sources

states.g2hcfg: NANOSLEEP (retrying name_open of the keystore every 250 ms)
states.g2happ: REPLY (its 7th request is held by cfgd)

g2h.culprit: cause outside the sources: no process named g2hkeys (keystore) is started; cfgd.c waits for it from request 6 on
g2h.fix: start the keystore service (or make cfgd fail the request when the keystore is absent)

g6b.row_text: missing_reply (plain): one code path receives and never replies

axes.trap: comment 'nothing to report back'

g6b.culprit: pwrmgr.c: case KEEPALIVE sets reply = 0, so the keep-alive request is never replied
g6b.fix: reply to the keep-alive too (MsgReply with EOK), or send keep-alives as pulses

gph.row_text: unknown: single process ticks a few times, then spins on the CPU

axes.trap: cycle only after move-to-front is enabled

gph.culprit: lru.c touch(): moves a node to the front without unlinking it, creating a cycle; find(-1) then never ends (round 6)
gph.fix: unlink p from its predecessor before p->next = head

grp.row_text: priority_chain: high client waits on a qd_fixed_chan server kept off the CPU by a middle load

axes.trap: the load keeps ticking

states.grpimu: READY (prio 6, fixed-priority channel, holds fc's request)
states.grplog: READY (CPU load at 16, ticks every 200 ms)

grp.culprit: imud.c: qd_fixed_chan server at 6 is starved by logfmt at 16 while fc (32) waits for its reply
grp.fix: use an inheriting channel for imud, or raise imud above logfmt

k74.row_text: missing_reply (plain): one code path receives and never replies

axes.trap: comment says other types belong to the resource-manager side

k74.culprit: audiod.c: 'if (m.type != QD_MSG) continue;' drops the volume message without replying
k74.fix: handle QD_VOLUME, or at least MsgError(rcvid, ENOSYS) for unknown types

kk5.row_text: deadlock: thread sends to a channel of its own process that no thread receives on

axes.trap: a receiving thread exists, on the wrong channel

states.kk5nv: SEND (MsgSend on its own int_chid; no thread receives there)

kk5.culprit: nvstore.c flusher(): receives on ext_chid while main sends flush requests to int_chid
kk5.fix: have flusher call qd_receive(int_chid, ...) (or send flushes to ext_chid)

kp6.row_text: missing_reply: server replies for a few rounds, then stops replying on one code path

axes.trap: server and reader keep ticking; comment says the next commit acks the writer

states.kp6kv: RECEIVE (keeps serving reads and commit pulses)
states.kp6wr: REPLY (its 6th write was dropped by the compaction path)

kp6.culprit: kvstore.c commit pulse handler: on the 6th commit (dirty >= JOURNAL_MAX) it compacts and sets pending_write = 0 without MsgReply
kp6.fix: reply to pending_write (or keep it pending for the next commit) on the compaction path instead of clearing it

kts.row_text: healthy: thread sends to own-process channel, another thread receives and replies

axes.trap: self-send looks like a self-deadlock

states.ktsapp: REPLY (waits for io's reply, ~100 ms each)
states.ktsio: NANOSLEEP (100 ms fsync stand-in before replying)

mqj.row_text: healthy: looks stuck in one snapshot but keeps ticking

axes.trap: slow replies

mqj.culprit: none (slow replies: 350 ms each, comment claims a few ms)

nrp.row_text: deadlock: server pool exhaustion (every pool thread in a synchronous send back to a client waiting for the pool)

axes.trap: client comment says it drains so jobd never waits

states.nrpwa: SEND (phase-2 confirm to a client that is REPLY-blocked on jobd)
states.nrpc1: REPLY (commit held by a pool thread)

nrp.culprit: jobd.c worker(): on COMMIT it MsgSends to the submitting client's own channel before replying; the client only receives between its own requests
nrp.fix: reply to the commit first and confirm asynchronously (pulse/MsgDeliverEvent), or have the client receive in a separate thread

p5u.row_text: missing_reply: server replies for a few rounds, then stops replying on one code path

axes.trap: comments say a shed caller retries; ctl's retry path is never reached because MsgSend never returns

states.p5uctl: REPLY (7th request shed without a reply)

p5u.culprit: rated.c: inflight++ on every request but decremented only on the error path; from request 7 on the 'shed' branch continues without MsgReply/MsgError
p5u.fix: decrement inflight after each MsgReply, and answer shed requests with MsgError(rcvid, EBUSY) instead of dropping them

paa.row_text: unknown, info_insufficient: loop stops for a cause not in the sources
paa.culprit: cause outside the sources: /etc/calib/limits.cfg does not exist on the target
paa.fix: provide the limits file (or keep running on the defaults when it is missing)

qgj.row_text: priority_chain: high client waits on a qd_fixed_chan server kept off the CPU by a middle load

axes.trap: comment calls the fixed channel deterministic

states.qgjadc: READY (prio 5 on a fixed-priority channel, has ctl's request, never scheduled)

qgj.culprit: adcd.c: qd_fixed_chan at priority 5 keeps the server at 5 while serving ctl (30); bgcrc at 15 takes the only core from 1.2 s on
qgj.fix: use a normal (inheriting) channel for adcd, or raise adcd above the load / lower bgcrc below adcd

qsa.row_text: healthy: client/server exchange next to a non-messaging CPU load (one above, one below the server)

axes.trap: a spinning process in every snapshot

quy.row_text: unknown, info_insufficient: loop stops for a cause not in the sources
quy.culprit: cause outside the sources: the supervisor that posts /seqr_ctl's semaphore is not part of the scenario
quy.fix: start the supervisor (or wait with a timeout and report)

su9.row_text: healthy: looks stuck in one snapshot but keeps ticking

axes.trap: looks exactly like a missing reply in one snapshot

states.su9evq: RECEIVE (holds the poll until the next 300 ms pulse)

su9.culprit: none (long poll replied on every timer pulse)

tzy.row_text: deadlock: two mutexes taken in opposite order by two threads

axes.trap: rotation only every 5th round, so both threads tick first

tzy.culprit: logrot.c rotate(): rotation path (n % 5 == 0) locks file_mx then buf_mx, while ingest() and the normal path lock buf_mx then file_mx
tzy.fix: take buf_mx before file_mx on the rotation path too (one lock order everywhere)

u7z.row_text: deadlock: two mutexes taken in opposite order by two threads

axes.trap: a watchdog thread keeps ticking, so the process looks alive

u7z.culprit: sessmgr.c reaper(): on the expiry path it holds sess_mx and then locks tbl_mx; login() locks tbl_mx then sess_mx
u7z.fix: on the expiry path release sess_mx and take tbl_mx first (tbl then sess), or unlink under tbl_mx only

vej.row_text: priority_chain: low thread holds a mutex without priority inheritance while a middle thread runs

axes.trap: middle thread keeps ticking; comment defends PRIO_NONE

states.vejctl: MUTEX (prio 30, waits for q_mx held by uplink)
states.vejupl: READY (prio 5, holds q_mx, never scheduled while compress runs)
states.vejcmp: READY (prio 15 CPU-bound compression; preempted only by the observer's pidin)

vej.culprit: telemd.c: q_mx is created with PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE; uplink (5) posts batch_ready while holding q_mx, compress (15) then runs ~60 s and ctl (30) blocks on q_mx
vej.fix: use the default PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT (or a priority ceiling) for q_mx, and/or post batch_ready after unlocking q_mx

ya8.row_text: healthy: mutex held for a long time by design, every loop keeps ticking

axes.trap: reader is MUTEX-blocked in almost every snapshot

states.ya8snp: NANOSLEEP (sleeps 350 ms while holding cfg_mx, by design)
states.ya8rd: MUTEX (waits for cfg_mx most of the time; NANOSLEEP in the short gaps)

ya8.culprit: none (cfgsync.c snapshot() holds cfg_mx for 350 ms by design)

zte.row_text: deadlock: ring of synchronous sends, every member TICKs before its first send

axes.trap: comments justify send-first as bounded memory

states.ztecola: SEND (MsgSend downstream; every member sends before it receives)
states.ztemrga: SEND (MsgSend downstream; every member sends before it receives)
states.ztecolb: SEND (MsgSend downstream; every member sends before it receives)
states.ztemrgb: SEND (MsgSend downstream; every member sends before it receives)

zte.culprit: collector.c and merger.c: qd_send(next) before qd_receive(chid); ring cola->mrga->colb->mrgb->cola
zte.fix: receive and forward in different threads, or make one hop asynchronous (pulse) so the ring cannot close
